name: Duplicate QT0.1 — Duplicate of Rejected Claim (Reject & Adjust → PX_RADJT0) Navigator
description: Resolve the PX_DP1/PX_QT0 hard edits flagging a potential duplicate of a history claim that was Resolved-Denied (rejected for authorization): confirm the LOB via Product, identify the electronic receipt method from the DCN camera reel, rule out corrected-claim events, compare the duplicate claim, verify the history claim was processed correctly, identify a partial match, note the current claim's rendering provider and review the history claim's rendering provider via Search, rule out the VA-Veterans-Georgia case, rule out every SOP claim scenario and confirm no additional-information attachments, rule out the PX_HPD Medicaid-reclamation event, confirm the multiple-units/date-range criteria do not apply, validate the related claim is Rejected, confirm via the Payment Information finalization code that it was denied for authorization (now available), cross-verify that authorization on the current claim via Claim Data → Review, then reject the current claim with code PX_RADJT0 and adjust the original.

steps.name: Identify the PX_DP1 and PX_QT0 hard edits
steps.description: The app will display all edits in the Event Resolution tab, with the PX_DP1 and PX_QT0 hard edits highlighted with an error indication — these are the current events to resolve. PX_QT0 indicates a possible duplicate of a rejected claim: complete the duplicate review before deciding.
steps.hint: Open the 'Event Resolution' tab. The PX_DP1 and PX_QT0 edits are active and highlighted in red.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the PX_DP1 and PX_QT0 hard edits

steps.name: Check the Line of Business via Product field
steps.description: Determine whether the claim is ITS or another Line of Business (LOB) by navigating to the Member Information tab, then the Group Information section, and reviewing the Product field. For ITS claims, the Product field may display values such as Local, National, or ACA. If the Product value is not Local, follow the alternate guidelines. If the Product value is Local, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Product is Local; therefore, the trainee may proceed. Also determine whether the claim was received electronically (alphanumeric) or by paper (numeric) by inspecting the DCN number
steps.hint: Open 'Member Info' and read the Product field under the Group section — it reads 'Local'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Member Info tab to read the Product field.
steps.checklistItem: Check the Line of Business via Product field

steps.name: Check for corrected claim events (PX_PAJ/PX_SCB)
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains corrected claim events by looking for PX_PAJ or PX_SCB events in the Event Resolution tab. If corrected claim events are present, follow the corrected events guidelines; if absent, proceed. In this scenario, the claim does not contain corrected claim events, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Return to 'Event Resolution' and scan the All Edits list — there are no PX_PAJ or PX_SCB corrected-claim events.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee revisits the Event Resolution tab to rule out corrected-claim events.

steps.name: Trigger the duplicate-claim comparison
steps.description: Obtain the potential duplicate claim(s) by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Duplicate sub-tab. Review the list of potential duplicate claims displayed in the table. Select the applicable duplicate claim using the radio button in the first column, then click Compare Claim. Once the comparison is initiated, a new section titled Claim Compare Results will appear below the duplicates table. Within this section, review the Show Differences subsection to identify and evaluate any differences between the current claim and the selected potential duplicate claim.
steps.hint: Open Claim Data → Duplicate, select the duplicate line's radio, then click 'Compare Claim'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee selects the duplicate radio and clicks Compare Claim (dispatches the compare_claim action).

steps.name: Confirm the claim appears to be a duplicate
steps.description: Review the Claim compare results under the Show differences section, checking Tax ID, Group or Provider name, Rendering provider or license number under the Provider information section, and Attachments under attachments section. The basic identifiers are shared, so the claim is initially flagged as a duplicate — the differences appear in the Provider accordion (rendering address, billing number, pricing ZIP) and the Claim Lines accordion (modifier). Expand the accordions to confirm.
steps.hint: Expand the Claim Compare Results accordions — the Provider rows (Rendering Address / Billing Number / Pricing ZIP) and the Claim Lines Modifiers row (blank vs RT) differ.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee reviews the compare-results accordions (dispatches review_duplicate).
steps.checklistItem: Confirm the claim appears to be a duplicate

steps.name: Verify the history claim was processed correctly
steps.description: Determine whether the history (duplicate) claim was processed correctly. Click the Open claim detail button to open the history claim. The system displays a message: "In real application, you need to follow guidelines to check if the history claim is processed correctly. In this scenario, consider this history claim is processed correctly." If the history claim was processed incorrectly, it must be adjusted before proceeding; if it was processed correctly, proceed. In this scenario, the history claim is processed correctly, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim, read the advisory message, then proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the history claim detail pop-up (dispatches open_claim_detail).
steps.checklistItem: Verify the history claim was processed correctly

steps.name: Identify a partial match
steps.description: Compare claim information between the current claim and the history claim across all relevant fields: Tax ID, Group or Provider name, Rendering provider or license number, Attachments, Date of service, Place of treatment, Procedure code, Modifiers, Diagnosis codes, National Drug Codes, Billed amount, and Units of occurrence. Note the values of these fields from both claims so you can compare them. To view them side by side, click Confirm match — the values from both the current claim and the history claim will be listed for review. If all fields match exactly, treat as a duplicate; if information only partially matches, proceed to deeper review. In this scenario, the information only partially matches (the rendering provider and the modifier differ), so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Open the Matching Duplicate Information panel — the Rendering provider / NPI and Modifiers differ, so this is only a partial match.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the matching-field list and sees the partial match (dispatches review_matching).

steps.name: Note the current claim's rendering provider
steps.description: Determine whether the rendering providers on the current claim and the history claim are different. First, note the rendering provider on the current claim. Go to the Provider Information tab and, under the Rendering section, check the Specialty Description. In this scenario, the Specialty Description is DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY.
steps.hint: Open Provider Info → Rendering and read the Speciality description — it reads 'DIAGNOSTIC RADIOLOGY'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Provider Info tab to read the current claim's rendering Speciality description.
steps.checklistItem: Note the current claim's rendering provider

steps.name: Review the history claim's rendering provider
steps.description: Now check the rendering provider on the history claim. Navigate to the Search tab → Claims sub-tab and click Search. The history claim is listed as a summary showing its details — Code, Name, From, To, Type, Provider, Bill Type, DCN, Charged, Paid, and Status. Directly below this summary, click the Open Claim Detail button. The history claim opens in the same layout as the current claim. Under the Rendering section of the Provider Information tab, note the Specialty Description — here it is RADIATION ONCOLOGY. Because the rendering providers are different, verify whether all of the remaining criteria match: same Tax ID, same Provider Group, same Specialty/Subspecialty, same Date of Service, same Procedure Code, same Billed Amount, and no modifier or the same modifier (line level). In this scenario, the rendering-provider specialties differ (Diagnostic Radiology vs Radiation Oncology), so the criteria do not fully match — continue to the next step.
steps.hint: Open Search → Claims, click Search, then click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim — its rendering Speciality description is 'RADIATION ONCOLOGY', so the specialties differ.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim in Search → Claims (dispatches the open_prior_claim action).
steps.checklistItem: Review the history claim's rendering provider

steps.name: Check for VA Veterans Administration in Georgia
steps.description: Determine whether the claim was submitted by a VA Veterans Administration facility located in Georgia by navigating to the Provider Information tab, then the Billing section, and reviewing the Name field. Verify that the provider name displayed on the claim matches the provider name shown in the system. Claims submitted by a VA Veterans Administration facility will typically display a VA-related provider name. Next, review the National State field in the same Billing section to confirm the provider's state. If the provider is a VA Veterans Administration facility and the National State is GA (Georgia), follow the applicable guidelines. If either condition is not met, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Name field displays BEVERLY RADIOLOGY MEDICAL and the National State is CA; therefore, the claim is not from a VA Veterans Administration facility in Georgia, and the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.hint: Open Provider Info — the Billing Name is 'BEVERLY RADIOLOGY MEDICAL' and the National State is 'CA', so this is not a VA Veterans hospital in Georgia.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Provider Info tab to check the billing name and national state.
steps.checklistItem: Check for VA Veterans Administration in Georgia

steps.name: Rule out claim scenarios and check for additional information
steps.description: Determine whether any SOP claim scenario applies — Surgeries, Modifiers, ACA California HMO Encounter, QCM event, Ambulance, Procedure code 62270, or Administration services (90460-90461); if a scenario applies, follow the linked section. In this scenario, none of the listed scenarios apply. Then check and validate whether the claim contains any additional information that was previously requested on the related claim — navigate to the Attachments tab and also review the Claim Image. If additional information is present, follow the relevant guidelines; otherwise proceed. In this scenario, no claim scenario applies and the claim does not contain any additional information, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Open the 'Attachments' tab — no SOP claim scenario applies and the claim carries only the PWK entry, with no additional-information documents.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Attachments tab to rule out claim scenarios and confirm there is no additional information.
steps.checklistItem: Rule out claim scenarios and check for additional information

steps.name: Check for the PX_HPD event (Medicaid reclamation)
steps.description: Determine whether the claim is a Medicaid reclamation claim by looking for the PX_HPD event in the Event Resolution tab. If the PX_HPD event is present, follow the Medicaid claim processing guidelines; if absent, proceed. In this scenario, the claim is not a Medicaid reclamation claim, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Return to 'Event Resolution' and scan the All Edits list — there is no PX_HPD Medicaid-reclamation event.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee revisits the Event Resolution tab to rule out the PX_HPD event.
steps.checklistItem: Check for the PX_HPD event (Medicaid reclamation)

steps.name: Check multiple-units and date-range criteria
steps.description: Check if the criteria below matches the claim. The services are billed with a procedure code that can have multiple units. Navigate to units’ field for line 1 under the claim lines tab. Services are billed with multiple units. The Julian dates are in consecutive order. The first 5 characters on the DCN are the Julian dates. The current claim does not match the above criteria, proceed to the next step. Then determine if the claims are billed with a date of service range and the claims processor is unable to verify the exact dates of service for when the services were performed. In this scenario, the claim has single units and the criteria do not apply, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Lines tab to check the units and date-range criteria.

steps.name: Verify the related claim status (rejected)
steps.description: Validate whether the related claim is finalized or open by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Duplicate sub-tab-->Radio button-->Compare claim button-->Review Claim Compare Results-->Open Claim Detail-->Confirm match button. After confirming the Matching Duplicate Information, locate and select the Check Related Status button positioned below the Matching Duplicate Information section. The history claim's status will then be displayed. A status of Pending-Investigation indicates that the related claim remains open. A status of Resolved-Denied or Resolved-Paid indicates that the related claim has been finalized, either as denied or paid. In this scenario, the related claim's status is Resolved-Denied, indicating that the claim has been finalized and denied. Therefore, the trainee should proceed to review the denial reason.
steps.hint: On the Duplicate sub-tab, click 'Check related status' — the history claim is Rejected (Resolved-Denied).
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee checks the related claim status (dispatches review_related_status).

steps.name: Verify the denial reason is authorization
steps.description: Validate the reason for the denial of the related claim. In the Search tab → Claims sub-tab, click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim to reopen its detail pop-up, then click the Finalization Code Detail button under the 'Finalization Code — Related Claim Denial Reason' section; read the description that appears to determine the denial reason (for example, code PX_R15270). If the denial reason is authorization-related, check whether the authorization is currently available on the current claim. In this scenario, the related claim was denied for authorization and the authorization is now available on the current claim, so the trainee proceeds to reject the current claim and adjust the original.
steps.hint: Open Search → Claims → 'Open Claim Detail', then click 'Finalization Code Detail' — code PX_R15270 was denied for Authorization, which is now available on the current claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Finalization Code Detail modal inside the history-claim Open Claim Detail pop-up (dispatches review_finalization_code).
steps.checklistItem: Verify the denial reason is authorization

steps.name: Cross-verify the authorization on the current claim
steps.description: Before proceeding with rejection, cross verify the authorization present on the current claim on Claim data tab > Review sub-tab. Navigate to the Claim Data tab, then the Review sub-tab, and read the Authorization section, which lists the Authorization #, Date Range, Procedure, Provider, Status, Svc type and Score of every authorization on file for the current claim. Confirm that an authorization covering the billed service is present and that its Status is approved. In this scenario the current claim carries authorization 6509985983 for procedure G0279 over the date range 03/27/2026–03/27/2026 with a Status of Approved, which confirms that the authorization the related claim was denied for is now available on the current claim, so the trainee proceeds to reject the current claim and adjust the original.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Review' and read the Authorization section — authorization 6509985983 for procedure G0279 is on file for this claim with a Status of Approved, so the authorization is now available.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Review sub-tab inside Claim Data to cross-verify the authorization on the current claim.
steps.checklistItem: Cross-verify the authorization on the current claim

steps.name: Reject the current claim with code PX_RADJT0
steps.description: Use the operational guidelines to adjust the original rejected claim, and reject the current claim using rejection code PX_RADJT0. Navigate to the Actions menu, select deny claim, enter PX_RADJT0 in the rejection code field, and confirm to capture the rejection.
steps.hint: Open the Actions menu, choose Reject, and enter rejection code 'PX_RADJT0'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee captures the reject code PX_RADJT0 via the Reject panel (dispatches deny_claim).
steps.checklistItem: Reject the current claim with code PX_RADJT0

steps.name: Submit the Reject decision
steps.description: Navigate to the Decision section in the header, select 'Deny' from the dropdown menu and click Submit to finalize the Reject decision and complete the attempt.
steps.hint: In the Decision section, select 'Reject' and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Reject decision with the Submit button.
